title: An ISO date (2026-03-15) is cleaned into a different valid date (26.03.2015) with no mark; a 3-digit year becomes 2020 with no mark
evidence: normalDate('2026-03-15') = '26.03.2015'; cleanReading date '2026-03-15' -> '26.03.2015', unsure_fields has no 'date' (past date, valid). '15.03.202' -> '15.03.2020', unmarked. '10:30, 15.03.2026' -> null (time read as day.month).
cause: The unanchored /(\d{1,2})\D+(\d{1,2})\D+(\d{4}|\d{2})/ takes the first day-month-year-looking run: in YYYY-MM-DD it starts at the year's last two digits and takes the day's two digits as a 2-digit year; (\d{4}|\d{2}) falls back to 2 digits of a 3-digit year. The future-date check cannot catch either because the result is in the past.

title: Every digit in the ward text is joined into one number: 'Ward 7 (Zone 6)' becomes ward 76, 'Ward 12, Zone 3' ward 123, both unmarked
evidence: cleanReading ward 'Ward 12, Zone 3' -> 123, '12/3' -> 123, 'Ward 7 (Zone 6)' -> 76; none adds 'ward' to unsure_fields. Only joins that land above 200 are caught.
cause: const wd = digits(r.ward); Number(wd) strips all non-digits and concatenates; it should take the first number (or mark the field when there is more than one). A wrong ward files the petition to the wrong zone and case.

title: Tamil digits (௯௦…) and full-width digits are silently dropped: the mobile, pincode or ward becomes empty with no doubt mark
evidence: mobile '௯௦௦௦௦௧௨௩௪௫' -> null, no 'mobile' mark; '９０００１２３４５' -> null, no mark; pincode '௬௦௦௦௧௧' -> null, no mark; ward 'வார்டு ௭௦' -> null, no mark. Same digits() is used by track.ts mayTrack, so a last4 typed in Tamil digits never matches.
cause: digits() is replace(/\D/g, '') without the u flag and without mapping U+0BE6-0BEF / U+FF10-FF19 to 0-9, and the 'mark it' branches only run when some ASCII digits survive.

title: A whole Aadhaar number read into the mobile field is kept in full (stored in petitions.reading and shown on the check screen)
evidence: cleanReading mobile '2345 6789 0123' -> mobile '234567890123' (whole number, marked unsure but kept). mobile '9123 4567 8901' -> '2345678901' (10 of 12 digits, after +91 stripping). The file header promises 'A whole Aadhaar number never leaves this file'.
cause: mobile goes through tenDigits() only; every text field goes through maskAadhaar but the mobile does not, and a 12-digit value is shown and stored rather than masked or dropped. readOne writes JSON.stringify(r.reading) to petitions.reading.

title: maskAadhaar misses common written forms: '9999 - 4512 - 7731', '9999/4512/7731', double spaces, zero-width space, Tamil or full-width digits
evidence: All six forms pass through cleanReading full_text unmasked. The same regex guards filePetition (officer-typed fullText/problem/subject) and paddle.ts, so the officer path and the PaddleOCR backup path leak the same way.
cause: AADHAAR = /(?<!\d)(\d{4})[\s.-]?(\d{4})[\s.-]?(\d{4})(?!\d)/g allows at most one separator from [\s.-], ASCII digits only, no / and no format characters (U+200B is not \s).

title: A mobile written as +919000012345 in the petition text is masked as if it were an Aadhaar number
evidence: maskAadhaar('Cell: +919000012345') = 'Cell: +XXXX XXXX 2345'. The full text the department reads loses the petitioner's number.
cause: Any 12 contiguous digits match; a leading + or '91' followed by [6-9] is not excluded.

title: The same person's online complaint on the same problem is reported as 'an earlier petition on other problems' and can never be offered as the case to join
evidence: judgeRepeats with an online match (dept: null, same mobile, same 'Sewage overflowing' line) -> headline 'This person has written 1 earlier petition on other problems.', sameProblem false, attachTo null.
cause: findRepeats maps every online complaint with dept: null (it even selects d.name AS dept_name and drops it); judgeRepeats requires sameDept for sameTopic, so online matches are never sameProblem, and the headline wording calls them petitions.

title: With no street read, any earlier petition with the same name is 'this person': a stranger in another ward gets 'this person's second petition' and their case is offered
evidence: Candidate R. Kumar, no mobile, no street, ward 70; earlier R. Kumar, other mobile, '5, Anna Salai, Adyar', ward 176 -> headline 'This is this person's second petition on this problem...', attachTo the Adyar case.
cause: sameName = same squashed name && (!street || ...): an empty street skips the address test, and a different mobile on both sides does not count against it.

title: 'N other people have written' counts petitions, not people: one neighbour who wrote three times is '3 other people'
evidence: Three earlier petitions from one mobile 9000099999 -> '3 other people have written about this in the same ward.'
cause: others.length is used as the person count; matches are not grouped by mobile or name.

title: The fuzzy street match compares the street with the end of the stored address, which is the area, so a one-letter street misspelling only matches when no area was entered
evidence: Street 'Jawahar Steet' vs address '27, Jawahar Street' -> samePerson true; vs '27, Jawahar Street, Perambur' -> false.
cause: similarity(street, squash(e.address).slice(-street.length)) assumes the address ends with the street, but filePetition stores address as [door, street, area].join(', ').

title: A problem line in Tamil script never shares a topic, even with itself, so Tamil-written repeats are not caught
evidence: sameTopic('சாக்கடை நீர் தெருவில் ஓடுகிறது', same line, samePerson=true) = false; Tanglish works. The officer can edit the problem line, and online complaint titles are often Tamil.
cause: words() keeps only [a-z0-9 ] and turns every Tamil letter into a space, so the word set is empty.

title: The came-before check fetches earlier petitions by exact name, so the same person written 'R. Kumar' vs 'R.Kumar', in NFD Tamil, or with a zero-width joiner is missed when there is no mobile
evidence: On the SQLite store: judgeRepeats on the stored row says 'second petition on this problem' for all three spellings; findRepeats returns headline null for all three.
cause: WHERE ... p.name = ? uses the raw trimmed name; the squash/NFC matching in judgeRepeats only runs on rows the SQL already returned. Names are also stored un-normalised by filePetition.

title: A new build loses what the live case had: 'written about 1 time before' and its priority drop to 0 and 45, and a petition added to an online complaint's case is split into its own case
evidence: Live: recurrence_90d 1, priority_score 53; after websiteCases: recurrence_90d 0. Petition attached to INC-W-2026-300CCC (online) -> after rebuild its event is in INC-W-<its own code>, 2 incidents.
cause: petitionCase hard-codes recurrence: 0 (filePetition passes the count only to addCaseLive). websiteCases adds petitions before online complaints, so attachToCase finds no online case yet and addCase opens a new one.

title: Approval adds a petition to any case id it is given: a closed case, or another department's case (the existing test even attaches a Metrowater sewage petition to an Electrical case)
evidence: CMWSSB petition with attachTo 'INC-ELE-1' (lead_dept GCC-ELE, is_open 0, Closed) -> attached: true, member_count 2, case stays closed and Electrical. The complaint row goes to Metrowater; the case nobody opens. ManuDesk keeps a chosen attach while the match is still listed as same-person only, e.g. after the officer changes the department (ManuDesk.tsx:170).
cause: fileSchema checks attachTo only by regex; attachToCase checks only that the incident exists, not is_open, lead_dept or ward.

title: The public tracker returns the officer's free-text notes, so a note naming the petitioner and her mobile is shown to anyone with the slip number and last 4 digits
evidence: officer_steps 'send' note 'Spoke to Parvathi on 9000041873 at 27 Jawahar St' -> /api/track answer contains it ('Work done: ...'). track.ts header: 'The answer holds the status only, no personal detail.'
cause: trackView maps every history row's remarks to note, and withProgress builds those remarks from officer_steps.note and Collector reject notes verbatim.

title: An Aadhaar number typed into the door or street field is masked in petitions.address but stored whole in complaints.street_address, specific_location, petitions.area and the case's place_text
evidence: fields door '9999 4512 7731', street 'Aadhaar 9999 4512 7731, Jawahar St' -> '9999 4512 7731' found in the stored rows. The reader's own fields are masked by cleanReading, so this needs a person to type it; f.date (20 chars, unmasked) is a second such path.
cause: Only maskAadhaar(address) goes to petitions.address; the raw address and place go to complaints, petitions.area and (via petitionCase) the case.

title: The Manu tests check real behaviour, but only on well-formed input, and one enshrines a wrong attach
repro: Read clean.test.ts, repeat.test.ts, manu.sqlite.test.ts; compare with probes in tests/qa/pass5/probes/manu-logic/
evidence: clean.test.ts: only DD.MM / D/M/YY dates, single-number wards, ASCII digits, the three tidy Aadhaar forms; no ISO date, no Tamil digits, no Aadhaar in the mobile. repeat.test.ts tests judgeRepeats alone (db mocked), so the exact-name SQL prefilter (manu-logic-12) and the online mapping (manu-logic-07) are never exercised. manu.sqlite.test.ts:307-312 attaches a CMWSSB sewage petition to an Electrical street-light case and asserts it as correct; its Aadhaar test checks only fullText and problem.
cause: Tests were written from the happy path of the reading-test samples; edge input and the store query path are untested.
